summary: Miminegash Range Lights on PEI's west coast: masts in 1886, wooden towers in 1900; the front light still lit on the North Breakwater, the rear tower moved to private land.

structures.type: square skeletal mast with trapezoidal daymark
structures.note: Present front light on the North Breakwater pier; daymark white with a red vertical stripe (Rowlett).

structures.type: square wooden tower with sloping sides
structures.note: Stood on the outer end of the south breakwater (Marine report 1900). LHF gives 17 ft to the lantern ventilator. Removed in 1972 (Rowlett).

structures.type: square wooden tower with sloping sides
structures.note: LHF gives 27 ft (8.2 m) high, elevated 28 ft (8.5 m) above high water. Sold in 1969 and relocated to private grounds near Kildare (Rowlett; LHF).
Rowlett's entry for the later rear light: 13 m (43 ft). Inactive since 2017 and later removed (Rowlett).

access.note: Front light: pier walkable, site open, tower closed (Rowlett). Rear light: privately owned, grounds and tower closed (LHF).

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (front light; owner/site manager per Rowlett). Rear tower on private land (LHF).

events.note: Pair of range lights established on masts to guide mariners into the pond (LHF; Rowlett gives 1886 as the station's establishment).
Patrick O'Brien appointed to the Miminegash Range Light, 14 May 1897; Frederick Costain to the Rix Point range light, 19 May 1897 (Marine tables).
New wooden towers built for the front and rear lights; lanterns on masts replaced by lights in enclosed towers (Marine report, fiscal 1900; LHF gives cost $254.30).
Front light red sector changed to cover the approach from the south (Marine report, fiscal 1902).
Elijah Costain appointed to the Miminegash inner light, 18 May 1906 (Marine 1910 keeper table).
Square wooden rear tower built in 1900 sold and relocated (Rowlett); LHF places it on private grounds near Kildare.
Square wooden front tower removed (Rowlett). The record gives 1972 as 'deactivated'; see corrections.
Range discontinued in 2017; front light still listed by the CCG as a light (Rowlett; CCG list).

corrections.why: Rowlett's entry for the present front light gives 'focal plane 4 m (13 ft)'. The record's 13.0 appears to convert 13 ft into metres as if it were metres.
Rowlett: the rear range light is 'Inactive since 2017 and later removed'. Its 1900 wooden tower was sold in 1969 and moved to private grounds near Kildare (Rowlett; LHF).
Rowlett says the second, square wooden front tower 'was removed in 1972'; the range itself was discontinued in 2017 (Rowlett). The record's 1972 event is an event for the tower, not the range.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The distance of more than 500 m comes from LHF's coordinates for the rear tower, which sits at Kildare where the 1900 wooden rear tower was moved (LHF; Rowlett). The OSM points and the CCG list position (46 52 49.0 N, 064 14 06.9 W) are the North Breakwater light at Miminegash. The rear tower's current location is Kildare, not the pond shore.

'Active' (CCG list; Rowlett) and 'deactivated' (Wikidata; Rowlett's range entry) both hold: the range was discontinued in 2017 (Rowlett), but the North Breakwater light is still listed by the Canadian Coast Guard as a light.

notes_for_editor: Thin-to-moderate station, Canada. Primary sources are the Department of Marine annual reports in the corpus (1900, 1902, 1910, and the report published 1912); the corpus has no volume for 1886 to 1899, so the 1886 date rests on LHF and Rowlett. The keeper tables give names and appointment dates; column alignment was matched by position in the OCR. Names matched by position: O'Brien (1902 scan 246, 'O'Brien, Patrick Miminegash Range Light May 14, 1897'), Frederick Costain (1902 scan 246), Elijah Costain (1910 scan 255), and the 1912 list (scan 241, names adjacent, no station column matched). The 1905-06 table (scan 346 of 1906v40i9p21_0345) prints 'Costain, Harold F' beside names whose station column was not matched, so it is not used; a checker should look at the page image. Open conflicts: (1) the 1900 front tower stood on the south breakwater (Marine 1900) but the present front light is on the North Breakwater (CCG; Rowlett); the sources do not explain the move. (2) Harold Frederick (LHF) vs Frederick (1902 table) for the rear keeper. (3) The record's focal height 13.0 m (corrected to 4.0 m per Rowlett) and the 1972 'deactivated' event (corrected to removed per Rowlett). (4) The 1900 tower heights (17 and 27 ft) and the $254.30 cost are LHF's transcription of the 1900 report, not confirmed in the corpus OCR; the story gives the heights as LHF's figures. (5) The LHF keeper names other than O'Brien and the two Costains come from LHF only and are marked so in the keepers list. The Marine report's 'Milton Walsh' supervision detail (LHF) was not found in the corpus and is not used. The PEI heritage blog and Wikipedia were not cited; Wikipedia was used for leads only. The CCG list edition date is not printed in the page read; it is the list as currently published on the CCG site. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the keeper tables were read from the page images. 1902 (scan 246, printed p. 69): 'Costain, Frederick, Miminegash, Rix Point Range Light, May 19, 1897' and 'O'Brien, Patrick, Miminegash Range Light, May 14, 1897' are on the same row. 1910 (scan 255, printed p. 253): 'Miminegash, Inner, Elijah Costain, May 18, 1906' and 'Outer, Patrick O'Brien, 14, 1897'. 1911 (scan 241, printed p. 234): the same two rows as 'Miminegash, Inner' and 'Outer'. The story now gives the heights in metres first, the Rix Point distance in km, and cites LHF for the inner (rear) keeper. The owner and site-manager wording follows Rowlett, not the CCG list, which gives the name and characteristic only.
